A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework. All 21 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training results, benchmark evaluations, reward-model comparisons, ablations, and human-annotation analyses in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds 14B model evaluations, training-method comparisons, and a constraint-level QwQ-32B judge experiment.

M1.justification: The incremental constraint curriculum, pseudo-label construction, binary reward-model training, hard/soft reward aggregation, and GRPO procedure remain unchanged. The added constraint-compatibility explanation describes the taxonomy and flexible generation prompt already present in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic instruction, mathematics, and science training coverage, eight instruction-following benchmarks, and six general-capability benchmarks. Additional model sizes and comparison methods do not introduce new tasks or domains.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates SFT, Self-Rewarding, and ProxyReward against the proposed method on two 7B models. Table 6 adds constraint-level QwQ-32B alongside the retained instruction-level judge. Appendix Tables 17–18 remove the Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-R comparator rows from v1 Tables 13–14. Self-as-Judge is described but has no identifiable reported result.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 14B configuration and shared-dataset method comparisons with CFR reporting. It also tests constraint-level QwQ scoring and uses that configuration as the speedup reference. Previously reported training budgets, data quantities, and AIME evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 and Appendix A.2.3 add a reward-granularity control comparing instruction-level and constraint-level QwQ-32B scoring. Existing curriculum and rule-reward ablations, human-versus-pseudo-label comparisons, consistency analyses, and training-dynamics plots are retained. The new robustness subsection mainly discusses existing evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain AIME Avg@30 sampling and the same shaded reward curves. v2 adds no repeated-training-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds 14B base/IF results, including IFEval 74.9/83.7, while Table 4 adds baseline scores and CFR entries. New constraint-level QwQ results in Table 6 reach 72.5/46.0/51.1 on the three policy benchmarks, exceeding the proposed reward model's retained 71.7/42.0/49.1. Reported speedups change from 115.0/119.0 to 126.5/123.7 because the reference judge changes; raw runtimes are unchanged. Appendix -R results are removed.

T1.justification: The curriculum definition, binary cross-entropy loss, hard and soft reward functions, and composite reward equation are unchanged. The revised adherence wording and expanded pseudo-label discussion introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: self-supervised instruction following, efficient constraint-wise reward modeling, out-of-domain generalization, and preservation of general capabilities.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions attribute gains primarily to reward learning and curriculum augmentation, explain pseudo-label noise tolerance, and interpret the QwQ comparison through reward density and efficiency. Section 4.5.2 replaces the restricted-search-space explanation for shorter distilled-model responses with improved efficiency. The WritingBench interference explanation is removed, and Section 4.4 narrows reward-model superiority to 7B comparators. Section 6 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents SFT teacher models and LLaMAFactory usage, specifies shared training data for the new comparisons, supplies complete Self-Rewarding and ProxyReward prompts, and explains the existing instruction-level QwQ scoring rule. Core reward-model/GRPO hyperparameters, hardware, and code-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Self-Rewarding, ProxyReward, and LLaMAFactory and expands its comparison with VERIF. References for Llama 3, GPT-4o, and QwQ-32B are removed although those models remain evaluated. Section 2 and the central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Sections 4.2 and 4.5 receive substantial rewrites and expanded explanations, while the reward-model ablation discussion is split into clearer topics. Appendices A.2–A.3 gain dedicated explanatory, scalability, baseline-method, and prompt subsections. These substantially expand the experimental narrative despite stable opening and concluding sections.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reflows the document with different page dimensions and text geometry, resizes and relocates displays, and enlarges Figure 7 from a column to a full-width figure. It adds a baseline-comparison table and three prompt tables and changes result-table membership. Most underlying figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The shared-data baseline comparisons, reward-granularity control, and explicit baseline prompts strengthen empirical assessment beyond v1. The improvement is moderated by inconsistent metric terminology and overstatements, including Appendix A.3.3's claim of consistent superiority to VERIF despite mixed outcomes in Table 3. The revision provides useful additional support without fully resolving the paper's reporting weaknesses.
